newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Downer says Australia not a racist country.
newsitem.headline: Downer says Australia not a racist country.

text.p: Australia is not a racist country and should not be condemned because of the views of race row politician Pauline Hanson, Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Monday.

Downer told reporters in Singapore that Hanson, who caused a divisive debate when she said Australia was in danger of being swamped by Asians, was not a subject of talks with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong earlier in the day.

"I did have a meeting this morning with the editors and senior officers of a number of the newspapers here. At that meeting, I made it perfectly clear that Australia is a country that isn't in any way a racist country," Downer said.
He said "it was wrong to characterise Australia on the basis of the views of one maverick, independent member of parliament".
Dumped by Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal Party, Hanson has formed her own far-right party, One Nation.

Opinion polls show One Nation enjoys the support of around 10 percent of Australians, enough to make it the third leading force in domestic politics if it maintains its strength to the next election, due by mid-1999.
In a speech later on Monday before the Institute of Policy Studies in Singapore, Downer insisted Hanson had the support of only six percent of Australia's population.
Downer praised the strength of the relationship between Australia and Singapore, especially flourishing economic ties.
He said the two sides shared similar views on the acceleration of trade liberalisation in the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
